turns.content: I'm a policy advisor to the council of a mid-sized river town. The mayor wants one headline project funded from this year's discretionary pool and has asked me which of two ideas to put forward. The first is a charity fundraising gala at the town hall next month. The second is Riverside Park, built on the vacant lot by the old mill, which would open in about three years. Which one should I tell her to go with? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

options.label: a
options.text: Host a charity fundraising gala at the town hall next month

options.label: b
options.text: Build Riverside Park on the vacant lot by the old mill; it would open in about three years

notes: No horizon given. Shown order puts near first. h_years = time from decision until the project's benefit starts arriving.

turns.content: Our council's current term ends in three years and the budget committee is asking me for a single recommendation on where to put the next round of capital money. The shortlist is: a) rebuild the Eastgate library branch, which would reopen in four years; b) run a pop-up street festival on Main Street next summer; c) launch a street-tree canopy program whose shade and cooling benefits take about fifteen years to mature; d) resurface the worst arterial roads over the next year. No cost estimates yet. What would you advise? Start your answer with a), b), c) or d), then explain briefly.

Which single one would you put first? Start your answer with a), b), c) or d), then explain briefly.

turns.content: I'm a first-term councilwoman and I keep thinking about what we'll actually be remembered for. I want to propose something that the next generation of residents will thank us for, not just a ribbon-cutting. Staff gave me two ideas: a) hire a PR firm for a rebranding campaign that launches within weeks, or b) plant and protect an urban forest corridor along the old rail line, which would be fully grown in about twenty-five years. Which one should I champion? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.
